dossier.summary: Stonegate Builders does residential remodels and small additions with about thirty people and a handful of crews.

peers.peer_group: construction firms with up to 50 people

data.headline: How mature are Stonegate's operations?
data.intro: Small remodeling firms often run on a few people who remember how every job goes. Three minutes shows how much of that is written down.

steps.title: Write down the steps of one job from quote to final walkthrough
steps.body: One page for the job you do most often. The next crew lead starts from it instead of from memory, and you see which steps slip.

steps.title: Keep job costs in one place and read them every Friday
steps.body: Put estimates, change orders and actual costs in one sheet or tool. Review it weekly so a job that runs over shows up while there is still time to act.

steps.title: Put change orders and scheduling reminders on rules
steps.body: Pick the two messages your office sends most each week and let software send them. It gives the office back time without adding a person.

steps.title: Name one person to own how jobs get run
steps.body: One owner, a short list, and an hour a week. In a firm of thirty, the owner usually holds this role without calling it that.
